license_note: Google serves Gemini 4 Argon as a managed model under the Gemini API Additional Terms of Service, which incorporate the Google APIs Terms of Service and a Prohibited Use Policy. Those terms prohibit developing competing models and reverse engineering, extracting, or replicating model components such as parameter weights, so nothing is licensed for self-operation. At this review date no model identifier or public API path is published, so the terms are recorded as the governing framework for the announced paid API release rather than as a documented per-model license.

license_evidence.scope: Access to Gemini 4 Argon through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio once released, including the incorporated Google APIs Terms of Service and Prohibited Use Policy; no weight license

access_boundary: This record represents the Gemini 4 Argon release announced September 30, 2026, Google's frontier model for coding, enterprise knowledge work, and defensive cybersecurity, distinguished by a 1M-token output limit raised from 64K. At this review date Google has published no model identifier, no API model page, and no deprecation date: access is restricted to invited Fairwind Program defenders and is stated to reach developers, enterprises, and consumers starting with paid API customers. The Gemini 3.8 Flash and earlier Gemini releases, the Fairwind Program itself, the Gemini consumer app, and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform are separate service, program, or model boundaries.
strengths: First-party announcement and a DeepMind model page with a published benchmark table, safety posture, and eval methodology
Announced introductory pricing of $2 per million input and $10 per million output tokens, with $4 and $20 applying after the introductory period
tradeoffs: No downloadable weights, and no published model identifier or API documentation at review time, so nothing can be pinned
Access is staged: restricted to Fairwind Program defenders now, with no announced general-availability date
